headline: Trump tells Ukraine to stop hitting Russian diesel
summary: Diesel in the US passed $6 a gallon on Friday, a record. On Sunday Trump said Ukraine should stop striking Russian refineries, which he blamed for a global shortage. Ukraine has hit Russia's oil industry for months, and Moscow banned diesel exports in July. The war on Iran cut shipments through the Strait of Hormuz too.

5-7.script: Big trucks run on a fuel called diesel, and right now there isn't enough of it, so it costs more. It's like when the store runs out of your cereal and the last box costs extra. Part of the reason is a war far away, and the president asked one side to stop hitting the other side's fuel. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: A five-year-old can hold "not enough" and "costs more." The war stays in the background, which is where it belongs at this age.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Ukraine has hit the refineries that make Russia's diesel because oil money pays for Russia's war. Russia ran short and stopped selling diesel abroad in July. The Iran war slowed tankers too, so the whole world is low and US diesel just passed $6 a gallon. Trump says pick other targets. It's like a water main: close one valve and every street loses pressure.
8-12.why: Kids this age can follow a chain with four links if each link is concrete. The water main gives them a picture for a global supply.

13-17.script: Ukraine hits Russian refineries because oil money funds the invasion. Trump wants it to stop: the world is short of diesel and US prices just passed $6 a gallon. Should a country under attack give up its best target because prices are rising elsewhere? And does it matter that he's asking with US voters heading to the polls in November?
13-17.why: Teenagers can weigh Ukraine's reasons against the price at the pump. Ask which one they'd put first, then tell them yours.

5-7.a: No. It's far away, across an ocean. This story is about fuel costing more, not about us being in danger.

8-12.a: Kyiv says Russia's oil pays for the war and fuels its army. Stopping the strikes would mean giving that up.

8-12.q: Why is diesel expensive here if the fighting is far away?
8-12.a: Diesel trades worldwide. Russia stopped exporting it in July, and the Iran war slowed tankers from the Gulf. Less supply everywhere means higher prices here.

13-17.q: Isn't Trump basically taking Russia's side?
13-17.a: He says he's protecting the world from a shortage. Ukraine says the strikes hit what pays for the war. Which reason weighs more to you?

13-17.q: Can he actually make Ukraine stop?
13-17.a: He asked. The report doesn't say what happens if Ukraine says no. Watch what Kyiv does this week.
